Hi, Emily.
How you doing?
Hi, how are you?
I'm good, I'm good, thank you.
Whereabouts are you today?
I'm in New Jersey.
I'm right outside New York City.
Ah, nice.
Yeah.
How about you?
I'm in Somerset.
Oh, cool.
In England.
I.
For some reason I thought you were English.
An English girl.
I don't know why I did think that, but there you go.
Nice to meet you.
So you are from New Jersey?
Yes.
Brilliant.
I love the New Jersey accent.
Are you good at it or.
You sound like you might be a bit posher.
The New Jersey action is usually like a New York accent.
Yeah, I guess.
Like a really broad one.
Yeah.
Cool.
All right, well, thank you for coming today and thank you for your time.
I do appreciate.
I don't know how it works with upwork normally, whether you have to do interviews or whether you just get paid to sit on a laptop or whatever.
Have you done much previous work on work?
Yeah, so I've been working with a few clients since maybe.
So I have a little bit of experience with upwork, but I'm always open to learning new things.
Yeah.
Cool.
All right, well, we'll get to that and I'll go through what it is that we're doing.
I guess what I'm keen to find out is just more about you and how you work and what work experience you've had so far.
So be great if you could tell me a little bit maybe from your time at college or university, if you went onwards and tell me, Yeah.
A bit about your experience.
Yeah.
So I was a communications and public relations major.
I went to a college in New Jersey.
It's called William Patterson.
And ever since I graduated, I had contract roles and internships in social media management, digital marketing and admin support.
And since I started freelancing on upwork, I've.
Oh, I'm sorry, your screen froze.
Sorry.
Yeah, I got you.
Oh, okay.
Yeah.
So ever since I started freelancing, I've been working with a few clients.
One of them is actually lead generation for a medical supplies company.
They purchase expired access or dead stock medical supplies.
So my role is to do outreach for their company and gather potential leads for them to purchase the expired supplies.
So I reach out to hospitals and healthcare facilities.
So that's I.
And I use Apollo to build lists of potential leads and send up email campaigns.
So that's one of the roles I'm working on right now.
Okay.
How many hours a week are you working with that client?
So right now I'm Looking for at least 10 to 15 hours.
Should you look for another 10 to 15.
Or possibly more?
Yeah.
Okay, cool.
All right, that's interesting.
So you're using Apollo already and how are you doing the actual outreach?
What are you using the sequence?
Yes, so it's.
I use the sequence.
I.
It's a mix of emails and phone calls.
So yeah.
Okay, cool.
And okay, so are you writing those emails or are you just putting campaigns together?
How does that part of it work?
So I create templates and then I use those templates to send out the emails.
So I have templates for everything.
Like I have one for outreach, one for follow up, one for interested clients.
I'm not interested, I guess.
Or do you just ignore them?
I'm not interested.
I, I just say thank you for your time.
Okay, cool.
So you send that templates.
All right.
But you're used to putting all of that together, basically building a campaign from scratch.
So now that's up and running.
Is that the only time that you've done it for that medical suppliers company?
Or do you, are you constantly building new campaigns to try and find different places for them to, to contact?
I'm sorry, what?
Well, so, so for us, we have every single client that comes in, they will have a campaign that's built for them.

So one person might be, in fact, it could be the same client might be looking to, to acquire companies that supply medical supplies, but they also looking at IT companies, they might be looking at wood shops, they could be looking at like five or six different things.

Each one we'd set up like a fresh campaign for them, you know, so we would have to find the leads, we'd have to find the leads with, with all of the buy box stuff in there, whatever it is, and then we'd have to, and, and send it out.

And then, then we manage those campaigns obviously, and we get results coming in and then we're responding to those leads as they come in and setting them up into the clients or one of our team members calendars to be screened as well.
So there's sort of a constant flow of campaign setup and management.
So I'm just asking you, do you, do you get to do a lot of that or have you just set it up the once and you're kind of just running that one campaign?
So so far my experience has been in the healthcare space, so pharmaceutical companies, hospitals, any healthcare facilities.
But I'm always open to learning about new industries and generating leads in other areas.
Okay, cool.
Your screen froze for a second.
Yeah, no, it Does.
Sorry.
That was definitely my, my connection.
I've got a satellite dish out in a field over there.
So I'm just.
I'm on top of a hill in the middle of nowhere.
So.
Okay, so.
Yeah, so I think.

So what I'm saying is have you, have you had to set up lots of these campaigns or have you just built the one for this healthcare client and you have to just keep maintaining the campaign to keep it going?
So right now I've only used the one campaign for this client.
Cool.
All right, no worries.
And then in terms of like the other stuff that you're doing, so I mean, the social media management and digital marketing stuff that you've done is.
Is that kind of now your skill set to basically do that for each client that you're.
You're looking to work with is sort of build them a marketing sort of process?
Yeah, I would love to gain more experience in digital marketing and social media.
I've had a few internships in it.
So, um, I managed the social media accounts.
I would generate content for them and I created an editorial calendar where I would plan out what I was going to post for the week and I would use tools like hootsuite to track the metrics.
Okay, brilliant.

So I don't know what it shows on my profile for upwork or anything that I've talked about, actually, but we are a company called Capital A and so the majority of our clients are actually marketing agencies.
So we buy and sell marketing agencies for our clients.
So this role in particular is not quite that, but the majority of work that Capital A does as a business is marketing agency related.
So the fact that you've got knowledge of that is pretty good because some clients are only looking to buy marketing agencies.

The fact that you've worked within an agency and would know the difference between hootsuite and something else is definitely good, but it won't make up the majority of the work that we're doing at the moment.
But it's a skill set that I'm really keen to get into our business.
I would say probably 90% of the people who work in our company are marketing agency people and a lot of them quite senior as well.
So they've owned their own marketing agency.
Right.
Or they've been the CEO of a big agency themselves and they work with us to help buy and sell stuff.
So.
So yeah, that, that is definitely of interest as well.
The actual role that we're looking to, to fill is with a service that we have called Deal Engines.
And so what we're doing is we are building a deal flow system for our clients.
So because we're so good at it.
My background is marketing myself, but I've got into the world of M and A, which is mergers and acquisitions.
And my specialism has been around the stuff that I'm good at, the stuff that I know, which is marketing and medium, record labels and TV companies, stuff like that.
That's what historically we've sold.
We have like a real focus on marketing agencies, but as we've grown, we've become really good at doing what we do for ourselves and for our clients.
So deal engines really is a platform where other companies that are doing what we do can now have a deal flow engine built for them.
We get them up and running.
So we build the campaigns, we find leads and we put everything inside the deal engine and then give it them to run on their own.
After a three month period, either they run it on their own or we carry on working with them.
But we work as an M and a advisory almost inside that.
So your role would be helping us get each of these campaigns set up.
So we're finding the leads, we're building all of the copy.
Right.
And getting the whole system set up.
We've got a piece of kit that runs through LinkedIn and cold email.
We're going to add in SMS and WhatsApp as well at some point.
But basically we'll be able to run a marketing campaign for each of our clients through several steps.
You know, trying to get them on LinkedIn, trying to get them on, on email, LinkedIn.
We already do.
We have a, I think a 30% response rate which is pretty high for our clients.
So they, they do get lots of responses.
But then we have to, we have to filter through them as well and make sure that they're not psychopaths, basically because you get people saying, oh yeah, I want that.
Right.
But our clients might not necessarily even want to speak to them.
So we have to make sure that they're qualified to sell their company and that they have a decent company and that it matches what our client is looking to buy as well.
So basically that's kind of the role.
Does that sound like something that you're looking to get involved in?
Yeah, that sounds great.
I would love to gain more experience in lead generation and marketing areas.
So that sounds like a perfect fit for my background.
Okay, brilliant.
All right, cool.
Is there any other questions around that or have I made it sound pretty straightforward?
So I have a few questions.
So what would a typical day in the role look like and is there, would there be a training period for it?
Sorry, I did miss your first question.
So you have a few questions.
Go on.
So, so I had a few questions.
So I, I was just wondering what does a typical day look like in the role and would there be a training period for it?
Okay, good question.
So a typical day would, would possibly be fairly varied.
We don't differentiate any of our team members as separate departments.
We are a fairly small team of about six, seven and everybody basically gets to work on the deals.
We're looking for people to, who want to get their hands dirty, who are passionate about results for their, for their clients.
I'm really, and we have suffered from this previously, we're not looking for, for people to kind of just go through the motions of ticking the boxes and follow our instructions.
What we're looking for is people that understand that the client wants to get a result.
We're marketing an opportunity to sell a company to targets and we get a lot of nutcases, like I say, responding.
Really what our client wants is somebody that is a bona fide business owner that can sell their business and that they have a great business.
And so everybody sits in the same team and that includes the people that go out and negotiate as well on behalf of our buyers or sellers and help them to get a deal done.
And so the opportunity is there for everybody to be involved in that process.

And if you are to be involved, particularly directly with helping somebody close a deal when it's one of our retained clients on the buy or the sell side and help them get a deal closed, then you get a piece of the commission as well, which can sometimes be hundreds of thousands of dollars, not the commission percentage, but certainly the whole commission that the company would get could be, you know, $250,000.
And so you would get a 5% on that as well.
If you can get the deal, help us get the deal closed.
So there's a much bigger opportunity.
But really like I say, I'm looking for somebody who's self sufficient and is able to handle a very, very day.

So obviously, you know, start the day we're looking to catch up on everybody's inboxes, make sure that, you know, any leads or deals that have come in that they've been responded to, if somebody's not a good fit, then we're able to get rid of them nicely.
And if somebody is a great fit, that we can qualify them as a potential seller.

And depending on what tier they are on, it would Also be potentially to have a call with that company as well and to just get some basic details from them, make sure that they're a human being that can breathe, you know, find out what the value of their business is, etc.
Etc.

And then we can put that into a document that then gets booked into our client's calendar and they get that document on their, you know, in their inbox so they can attend that call without having to do any research.
That's kind of it.
So like I say, you could be involved all the way to getting the deal closed at some point.
I think initially the larger focus would be on making sure that we've got everybody's inboxes up to date.

But certainly as we get more experienced and you get a closer experience with the clients, and especially if you're, you know, phone in targets and qualifying them as sellers, then the potential is to work alongside the clients to help them get deals closed as well.
Okay.
So, yeah, so it could become more interesting, it could become more about the M and A side of things over time.
And like I say, the majority of our clients are actually marketing agencies.
So the fact that you've got insight into that could be really interesting as well.
I know it's obviously not your passion.
It's probably doing, doing the marketing itself, but it would be talking to, you know, sometimes we talk to CEOs of, of companies that are doing like, you know, 20, 30, 50 million in revenue.
Yeah.
So that, you know, they're successful marketing agency founders that we're talking to as well.
So, so it can be very, very fun.
My team is based in, mostly in the UK and the us.
We do have a couple of team members in the Middle east or Asia as well.
But it's a, an international team and our business is completely international.
Oh, wow.
So I mean a lot of it is in the U.S. but you know, for instance we, we've got clients in Turkey and Hong Kong, Australia.
We sold an agency that was in Israel to an American company.
So we're kind of all over.
Wow.
Yeah.
So actually I had a question.
So I was wondering, are your clients mostly in UK or US or is it worldwide?
Yeah, so a lot of the deal engine clients are UK based because we actually acquired a company that was in the UK that already did this.
So basically we acquired a marketing agency that already did it and then we rebranded it as deal engines.
So a lot of the clients and the marketing, the way it's all set up is quite UK focused list, but the majority of capital a's clients are actually in the U.S. okay.
Yeah.
So it, it will be a mix, it will be a mix of that.
So the fact you're on the east coast is good for us because it's only a five hour difference.
There's a, a lot of an easier crossover.
But we have a lot of clients in California as well.
And actually Amanda, who is our partnerships director is in Texas as well.
She announced in Texas, which is in Dallas today, but she normally lives in Austin, although she's a New York New Yorker, I think.
And she did live in LA not so long ago.
So she's all over.
Yeah.
But we do have other team members in, in New York as well.
So Heather is in New York and John is in Denver.
So all over the place.
So actually I have one more question.
So I know you mentioned Apollo.
Are there any other programs that you use?
Yes, we have our own platform that we use that is completely rebranded as DL engines.
It does have a similar system where it is that system basically the same as Apollo.
It's not as corporate looking as Apollo, should I say.
It's.
It's a bit more of a simplified version of Apollo which has all of the tools and sequences and everything built in.
So it's a platform that we set up and run for our clients like a simplified version of it.
But we do also use Apollo a lot.
We use Apollo because it's actually better.
They've got cleaner data than our proprietary.
So what we tend to do is get the data from Apollo, clean it up and then put it into a campaign and let it run rather than use our own data, which is not as good.
Right?
Yeah.
So yeah, Apollo.
What else do we use?
We have used Clay, we also use wizard, we use LinkedIn, Sales Navigator as well.
We use wherever we can get it, basically.
Okay.
And we've also got our own CRM which, which is a platform called Close, which is not public facing at all.
But we've got 130,000 marketing agencies in there as well.
So we've got a lot of our own data already that we, we sometimes use.
So it's private.
Yeah, it's all private here.
So yeah, there's a lot of platforms to, to learn.
I mean we are basically a tech layer for other M and A advice, not advisors.
How would I put it?
We're a tech layer for other business buyers and sellers.
So yeah, there's, there's, there's probably not a lot to learn because you've already got Apollo as a skill.
So it's very.
Yeah, okay, cool.
All right.
I've got to hop on to my next call in five minutes, so I think that's probably everything I need, Emily, if you're happy.
Yeah.
So that's all the questions I have right now, but it was great meeting you and learning more about the role, and I would love to be considered for it.
Yep.
Brilliant.
And an absolute pleasure meeting you, Emily, and thank you for your time, and I will.
Yeah, I. I've obviously got a couple more.
More people to speak to, but I'll make a decision over the next day or so.
Would you be up for maybe doing a.
Like a trial?
Sure.
Yeah, that's.
That would be great.
That sounds great.
Yeah.
Okay.
Perfect.
All right, brilliant.
Enjoy the rest of your day.
I know it's still early where you are, so you got a whole day.
Yeah.
Thank you.
Have a good one.
Have a good one, too.
Bye.
Bye.
